Intro & Goal

The Dell Technologies Forum Podcast Series was created to extend the solution-driven conversations from Dell’s Forum events across EMEA.

The goal: position Dell as a thought leader, continue engaging customers post-event, and build a likeminded, innovation-focused community.

[video width="1920" height="1080" mp4="https://damienmulhall.com/storage/2025/09/3966-DEL-SD-Podcast-Series-for-DTF-Podcast-trailer-3-17May2024.mp4"][/video]

Challenges

  • Very tight deadlines: often just two weeks between guest introduction and publishing date.
  • Heavy pressure from senior teams to repeatedly cover high-priority themes, risking content repetition.
  • Ensuring consistent audio quality and maintaining listener engagement across all episodes.

Solution

  • Designed a refined guest preparation workflow: from intake to content coaching, technical setup, and production milestones.
  • Cross-referenced all guest talking points against prior episodes to avoid content duplication, and tactfully coached guests toward fresher, more engaging narratives.
  • Established a strict publishing process ensuring episode delivery, transcript accessibility, and organic social engagement through curated audio excerpts.

My Role

  • Oversaw content planning, script development, and guest management.
  • Coordinated recording logistics and ensured consistent audio standards.
  • Managed stakeholder communication, balancing guest needs with internal priorities.
  • Drove episode marketing through curated social media clips and visuals.
  • Maintained accessibility standards by delivering clean episode transcripts.

Results

  • Surpassed 100,000 downloads, outperforming other corporate podcast initiatives globally for Dell.
  • Maintained strong editorial integrity — no episodes retreaded content, despite internal pressures.
  • Consistently delivered episodes on time and across multiple platforms, driving listener trust and engagement.
post_excerpt: A corporate podcast extending event conversations and building an engaged community around innovation.

Intro & Goal

A leading technology solutions provider sought to engage 170 high-value customer accounts over three months, supporting their migration to Windows 11 and preparing organizations for future AI initiatives.

The goal: enable account executives to re-engage customers meaningfully through localized community workshops, reinforcing the provider’s leadership in enterprise IT solutions.

Challenges

  • Building real perceived value for busy IT leaders to attend full-day workshops.
  • Tight logistics: organizing seven events across different UK cities within a one-month period.
  • Brand and legal constraints requiring heavy revisions to campaign visuals and messaging.
  • Managing a tight $80k budget while meeting expectations for delivery and experience quality.
  • Handling dual funding partner requirements with separate proof of execution standards.

Solution

  • Established a clear project structure: defined roles, frequent internal checkpoints, and weekly client calls.
  • Designed and pitched campaign branding, messaging, and creative assets alongside an internal event specialist and creative director.
  • Built a central client-facing dashboard tracking all deliverables, budgets, and resourcing.
  • Collaborated closely with technical leaders to align event content with broader migration and AI readiness narratives.

My Role

  • Led the full project from concept to delivery.
  • Managed the complete campaign budget and monitored burn rates.
  • Oversaw creative development and approvals with brand and legal teams.
  • Delivered seven events on time, to high client standards, with full compliance to funding partner proof of execution processes.

Results

  • Successfully executed 7 community events across the UK.
  • Achieved 80% registrant-to-attendee conversion rate.
  • Received overwhelmingly positive attendee feedback post-events.
  • Generated $9.5 million in new pipeline directly attributed to campaign engagement.
post_excerpt: A series of UK-based workshops designed to engage high-value enterprise accounts and drive solution adoption.

post_content:
Intro & Goal

The Google for Education eGuide was designed as both a buying guide for K-12 school IT decision-makers and a quick-reference tool for sales teams. The objective: present an end-to-end view of Chromebooks, accessories, software, and education programs, structured around personas — from students of all age groups to teachers, administrators, and superintendents.

Challenges

  • Navigating complex brand and legal approval processes across Google and Dell stakeholders.
  • Balancing educational storytelling with strict factual accuracy and compliance requirements.
  • Framing workflows and solutions in a way that felt genuinely relatable and valuable to education professionals.

Solution

  • Applied a structured Waterfall project management approach, locking key approvals at each milestone: copy → design → publishing.
  • Conducted interviews with teaching specialists to deeply understand classroom workflows across different educational levels.
  • Designed visual matrices mapping educator workflows to recommended technology and software solutions, enhancing the guide’s practical value.
  • Maintained early and frequent communication with Google and Dell content specialists to ensure clarity, accuracy, and alignment.

My Role

  • Project managed the eGuide from kickoff through delivery.
  • Oversaw content development and creative production, coordinating with stakeholders and internal teams.
  • Managed all rounds of internal and external approvals.
  • Ensured full delivery within project funding and publishing deadlines.

Results

  • The eGuide became a hero reference asset for global Chromebook sales in the education sector.
  • Client re-engaged me three times over multiple years to update and extend the guide’s relevance as educational needs evolved.
post_excerpt: A persona-driven guide helping K-12 IT decision-makers and sales teams navigate Google’s complete educational technology ecosystem.

post_content:
Intro & Goal

Ahead of annual product launches (PCs, laptops, desktops, accessories, and displays), the client needed a structured training initiative to prepare sales teams across 40+ EMEA sites. The objective: create clear, engaging training materials and drive internal excitement through a coordinated hype campaign — ensuring teams were equipped to position the new generation of products effectively.

Challenges

  • Tight delivery timelines during final product development stages.
  • Very limited campaign budgets for collateral and distribution.
  • Managing stakeholder alignment and approvals across brand, legal, and marketing teams.
  • Navigating cross-border shipping and customs risks to ensure timely delivery of physical assets.
  • Balancing strict brand guidelines with creative, engaging campaign ideas.

Solution

  • Presented eco-friendly, brand-compliant merchandise options to streamline customs approvals and align with corporate values.
  • Developed a visually consistent, easy-to-use training manual highlighting product strengths and positioning strategies for sales teams.
  • Built a supporting hype campaign: launch emails, trainer kits, branded giveaways, internal videos, and session templates.
  • Maintained constant communication with internal stakeholders to accelerate approvals and mitigate delivery risks.

My Role

  • Project managed the full program lifecycle across all EMEA sites.
  • Oversaw content development, creative production, logistics, and stakeholder coordination.
  • Managed all approvals and ensured full compliance with brand and legal guidelines.
  • Delivered materials to each site with full usage guidance for local training managers.

Results

  • Successfully delivered training materials to 40+ EMEA sites each year on time and on budget.
  • Received strong positive feedback from sales managers and local training leads.
  • Client was awarded renewed budget annually and chose to re-engage me to run the project for five consecutive years based on consistent successful delivery.
post_excerpt: A regional sales enablement project delivering training materials and engagement campaigns to over 40 sites across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.

post_content:
Intro & Goal

The filmmaking guide was developed to serve as an organic social asset and lead generation tool, promoting Dell’s Precision workstations to media and entertainment SMEs. The objective: provide authentic, high-value content featuring Hollywood editor Vashi Nedomansky, to build credibility, drive marketing-ready leads, and challenge Apple’s dominance in the media production sector.

Challenges

  • Coordinating communication and approvals with a high-profile creative partner while maintaining strict delivery timelines.
  • Managing permissions and licensing rights to use well-known intellectual property (e.g., Deadpool references).
  • Navigating approval processes across Dell’s brand and legal departments.
  • Balancing creative integrity with marketing requirements and brand guidelines.

Solution

  • Applied an iterative project management approach to tightly control approvals: locked content before progressing to design phases, minimizing risk of scope creep.
  • Developed the primary output as an interactive HTML eGuide for U.S. campaigns.
  • Produced a secondary interactive PDF variant tailored for EMEA content syndication programs.
  • Maintained early, frequent collaboration with both Vashi’s team and Dell’s internal stakeholders to ensure aligned expectations and approvals.

My Role

  • Project managed the eGuide from kickoff through final delivery.
  • Oversaw content development, creative production, and stakeholder coordination.
  • Managed all internal and external approval rounds across creative and legal teams.
  • Delivered the full project within the required funding and publishing deadlines.

Results

  • Produced a highly engaging eGuide that resonated with the target media and entertainment audience.
  • Successfully approved for syndication in EMEA campaigns.
  • Earned strong praise from the project sponsor and marketing teams.
  • Vashi Nedomansky continues to feature the guide publicly on his website, click here>
post_excerpt: A hero marketing asset created to engage media and entertainment businesses and reposition enterprise solutions in a traditionally Apple-dominated segment.
